items.definition: In a 'neither...nor' construction, the verb agrees with the subject that is closer to it.
items.rationalization: In 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ the book,' the subject closer to the verb is 'students' (plural), so a plural verb is required. The same proximity rule applies in 'Either the musicians or the conductor ___ responsible for the error,' where the closer subject 'conductor' (singular) takes a singular verb.

mnemonic.title: Proximity Rule for Neither/Nor
mnemonic.phrase: The verb agrees with the closer subject
items: Neither A nor B → verb agrees with B
Either A or B → verb agrees with B

items.tosCompetency: Apply rules of subject-verb agreement in complex sentence structures

items.definition: Collective nouns such as team, committee, family, group, herd, staff, and board are treated as singular subjects when acting as one unit.
items.rationalization: In 'The team, along with their coach, ___ heading to the championship,' the subject is 'team' (singular), and intervening phrases like 'along with' do not change the verb. Similarly, 'The committee, including its youngest members, ___ reached a consensus' takes a singular verb because the committee acts as one body.

mnemonic.title: Collective Noun Rule
items: Intervening phrases don't change the verb
Only when members act individually = plural

items.tosCompetency: Use collective nouns correctly as subjects in sentences

items.definition: Indefinite pronouns like each, one, every, everyone, neither, and either are always singular and take singular verbs.
items.rationalization: In 'Each of the students ___ a unique perspective,' the subject is 'Each' (singular), not 'students.' Similarly, 'One of the students ___ already submitted the assignment' and 'Every one of the players ___ giving their best' require singular verbs. These pronouns are grammatically singular regardless of the prepositional phrase that follows.
items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with indefinite pronouns

items.definition: Uncountable (mass) nouns such as information, news, furniture, and mathematics take singular verbs.
items.rationalization: In 'None of the information ___ relevant to the case,' the subject 'information' is uncountable and takes a singular verb. Similarly, 'The news about the accident ___ shocking' and 'Furniture in the house ___ stylish' require singular verbs because these nouns have no plural form.
items.tosCompetency: Use uncountable nouns correctly in subject-verb agreement

items.term: Nouns with Plural Form but Singular Meaning
items.definition: Some nouns end in -s but are singular in meaning and take singular verbs, such as news, mathematics, physics, politics, and economics.
items.rationalization: In 'Politics ___ a complex subject to study,' the word 'Politics' ends in -s but is singular, so it takes 'is.' Similarly, 'Mathematics ___ a subject many students find challenging' requires a singular verb. These are exceptions to the typical plural -s rule.
items.tosCompetency: Identify nouns with plural form but singular meaning

items.definition: Phrases such as 'along with,' 'together with,' 'as well as,' and 'including' do not change the number of the subject.
items.rationalization: In 'The team, as well as their supporters, ___ ready for the final match,' the subject is 'team' (singular) because 'as well as' is not a conjunction but an intervening phrase. Similarly, 'The books, together with the notes, ___ missing from the shelf' takes a plural verb because 'books' is the true subject.

mnemonic.title: Intervening Phrase Rule
mnemonic.phrase: Ignore the extra, focus on the subject

items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with intervening phrases

items.definition: Quantifiers can be singular or plural depending on the noun they refer to; 'the number' is singular while 'a number' is plural.
items.rationalization: In 'Some of the furniture ___ damaged in the flood,' 'furniture' is uncountable, so the verb is singular. In 'Several of the pieces ___ damaged in the move,' 'pieces' is plural, so the verb is plural. 'The number of students ___ increasing' is singular, while 'A number of students ___ absent' is plural.
items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with quantifiers and fractions

items.definition: Two subjects joined by 'and' generally take a plural verb, unless they refer to the same person or thing.
items.rationalization: In 'Both of the twins ___ invited to the party,' 'Both' indicates two people, so the verb is plural. In 'A variety of topics ___ covered in the lecture,' 'topics' is plural, so the verb is plural. However, 'The president and CEO ___ attending' would be singular if referring to one person.
items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with compound subjects

items.definition: 'The number' is always singular and takes a singular verb; 'a number' is always plural and takes a plural verb.
items.rationalization: In 'The number of students in the class ___ steadily increasing,' 'The number' is the subject and is singular, so 'is' is correct. In 'A number of students ___ absent today,' 'A number' means 'several' and is plural, so 'are' is correct.
items.tosCompetency: Distinguish between 'the number' and 'a number' in subject-verb agreement

items.definition: Fractions and percentages take singular verbs when referring to a singular or uncountable noun, and plural verbs when referring to a plural noun.
items.rationalization: In 'Half of the cake ___ already eaten,' 'cake' is singular, so 'was' is correct. In 'Half of the students ___ absent,' 'students' is plural, so 'were' is correct. The noun after 'of' determines the verb.
items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with fractions and percentages

items.definition: In an 'either...or' construction, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it.
items.rationalization: In 'Either the books or the pen ___ missing,' the closer subject is 'pen' (singular), so 'is' is correct. In 'Either the pen or the books ___ missing,' the closer subject is 'books' (plural), so 'are' is correct. The proximity rule applies to both 'either...or' and 'neither...nor.'

mnemonic.title: Either/Or Proximity
items: Either A or B → verb agrees with B
Neither A nor B → verb agrees with B

items.tosCompetency: Apply the proximity rule in either/or constructions

items.term: Plural Nouns with Singular Verbs (Special Cases)
items.definition: Some nouns like 'pair,' 'series,' and 'herd' are singular in form and take singular verbs even when they refer to multiple items.
items.rationalization: In 'A pair of shoes ___ left in the hallway,' 'pair' is singular, so 'was' is correct. In 'A series of events ___ led to this conclusion,' 'series' is singular, so 'has' is correct. These nouns are treated as single units.
items.tosCompetency: Identify nouns that are singular despite plural-like forms

items.definition: 'None' can be singular or plural depending on the noun it refers to; it is often plural when referring to countable nouns and singular when referring to uncountable nouns.
items.rationalization: In 'None of the students ___ late for the exam,' 'students' is countable and plural, so 'were' is acceptable. In 'None of the information ___ relevant,' 'information' is uncountable, so 'is' is correct. The noun after 'of' determines the verb.

mnemonic.title: None Rule
mnemonic.phrase: None = not one (singular) or not any (plural)

items.tosCompetency: Apply subject-verb agreement with 'none'
